newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bank lending rises 9.4 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bank lending rises 9.4 pct in March.

text.p: Venezuelan commercial bank lending rose 9.4 percent in March to 2.6 trillion bolivars ($5.4 billion) from February, evidence of a significant rebound in lending, Softline consultants reported.

According to the firm's monthly round-up of 40 commercial banks, the banking sector's intermediation index -- which describes the amount lent per each bolivar deposited -- rose to 46.24 percent, even as the deposit base grew 1.4 percent to 5.3 billion bolivars.
The intermediation index "is at its highest level since mid-1994 and its rise is evidence of a rebound in credit provision," Softline said.
That level, however, is still well under over 100 percent intermediation rates in Colombia, Chile and Mexico, industry figures show.

Despite the rise in lending into an economy projected to grow four percent this year, Softline cautioned that there still remained a strong dependence on Central Bank-issued securities, called TEMs, in Venezuelan bank portfolios.

Ever since Venezuela's banking sector tanked in a 1994-5 financial crisis, banks have used high yielding TEMs, issued by the Central Bank to mop-up excess liquidity, to pad out portfolios while credit demand remained slim.

But in March, for the first time in months, total investments in securities -- at 2.5 trillion bolivars, or 36 percent of bank assets -- were less than loans outstanding which stood at 37 percent of bank assets, Softline said.
Softline added that bank capitalization rates, or the ratio of shareholders equity to total assets, edged ahead to 13.8 percent in March from 13.0 percent at the end of last year.
